_about: Plain-language labels for the oncologist report (scripts/build_report.py). Written by a senior heme-onc agent from rubric_v2.toml, case.toml and gold.json, then checked item by item against the rubric text by an independent heme-onc agent (2026-10-22). Not human-reviewed. Never shown to the model.

case_card.title: Double-hit lymphoma found after R-CHOP was planned
case_card.patient: 54M, ECOG 1, with a rapidly enlarging right cervical mass, dysphagia and morning facial fullness; 12.0 cm anterior mediastinal mass with about 50% SVC narrowing, all disease above the diaphragm, LDH 740 rising to 812, uric acid 7.6 to 7.9, LVEF 60%. Node biopsy was signed out as DLBCL NOS (GCB, MYC 80%/BCL2 90% by IHC, Ki-67 95%), but the 9/19 FISH addendum shows MYC and BCL2 rearrangements after R-CHOP x6 had already been planned to start 9/22.
tests: The late FISH addendum changes the diagnosis to double-hit lymphoma (HGBL with MYC and BCL2 rearrangements), not DLBCL NOS.
The R-CHOP plan was written before FISH and must be replaced with intensive therapy such as DA-EPOCH-R x6 or a clinical trial.
Disease is stage II bulky (12 cm mediastinal mass, above the diaphragm only), not stage III or IV.
IPI and CNS-IPI are only 1, but double-hit biology drives the risk, so brain MRI, lumbar puncture and CNS prophylaxis are still needed.
Bulky mass, high LDH and rising uric acid need TLS prophylaxis; DA-EPOCH-R needs G-CSF every cycle and its 96-hour infusion goes through the new port.
case_card.correct_plan: Revise to double-hit lymphoma, cancel the R-CHOP plan and give curative DA-EPOCH-R x6 (or a trial) with G-CSF, TLS prophylaxis, baseline brain MRI and LP, CNS prophylaxis, sperm banking and SVC/airway precautions. Then interim and end-of-treatment PET-CT read with Deauville, with ISRT to the mediastinum decided at multidisciplinary review.

items.label: Revises diagnosis to double-hit lymphoma (MYC and BCL2 rearranged)
items.why: The FISH addendum overrides the DLBCL NOS sign-out, and this diagnosis decides the regimen and the CNS work-up.

items.label: Keeps the final diagnosis as DLBCL NOS or denies double-hit
items.why: Missing the double-hit result leads to standard R-CHOP and under-treatment of an aggressive lymphoma.

items.label: Notes GCB phenotype by Hans (CD10+, BCL6+, MUM1-)
items.why: Documents cell of origin; double-hit lymphoma with BCL2 rearrangement is typically GCB-type.

items.label: Recognises the 9/14 R-CHOP plan predates FISH and cancels it
items.why: Cycle 1 of R-CHOP is booked for 9/22; it must be stopped before he receives the wrong regimen.

items.label: Stages as Lugano stage II bulky (12 cm mediastinal mass)
items.why: All disease is above the diaphragm with no extranodal sites; the 12 cm bulk supports considering consolidative mediastinal radiotherapy.
items.checker_revised: The current why says bulk means he 'is treated as advanced-stage disease'. Lugano 2014 says stage II bulky is treated as limited or advanced depending on histology and other factors. In this patient the double-hit biology, not the stage, sets DA-EPOCH-R x6, so the statement overreaches and could mislead.

items.label: Assigns stage III or stage IV
items.why: PET shows no disease below the diaphragm and no extranodal sites, so this would be an incorrect stage.

items.label: Notes double-expressor IHC, but FISH double-hit is the key classification
items.why: MYC 80%/BCL2 90% protein expression is secondary; the rearrangements, not the IHC, drive treatment choice.

items.label: Calculates IPI 1 (LDH only); double-hit biology dominates the risk
items.why: A low IPI here is misleading; the rearrangements make outcomes poor with standard therapy.

items.label: Recommends DA-EPOCH-R x6 or trial; intensive alternatives acceptable
items.why: Double-hit lymphoma is not adequately treated by R-CHOP; a fit 54-year-old needs intensive curative therapy.

items.label: Recommends R-CHOP alone, or proceeding with the 9/14 plan
items.why: R-CHOP alone is not preferred for rearrangement-defined double-hit lymphoma and risks lower cure rates.

items.label: Recommends palliative-only care, best supportive care or hospice
items.why: He is fit, his goal is cure, and this lymphoma can be cured with intensive therapy.

items.label: Considers ISRT to the bulky mediastinal site
items.why: Radiotherapy can consolidate residual PET-positive disease in a 12 cm mediastinal mass.

items.label: Orders brain MRI and LP with CSF cytology and flow
items.why: Double-hit carries high CNS risk despite CNS-IPI 1; occult CNS disease would change the regimen.

items.label: Recommends CNS prophylaxis (intrathecal or high-dose methotrexate)
items.why: Reduces the high risk of CNS relapse that comes with double-hit biology.

items.label: Dismisses CNS risk as low; says no CNS evaluation or prophylaxis needed
items.why: A low CNS-IPI understates the risk; skipping evaluation or prophylaxis leaves CNS relapse unaddressed.

items.label: Plans end-of-treatment PET-CT read with Lugano/Deauville
items.why: Confirms complete metabolic response and guides biopsy or radiotherapy for residual mediastinal uptake.

items.label: States G-CSF is mandatory every cycle of DA-EPOCH-R
items.why: DA-EPOCH-R dose escalation depends on growth-factor support to limit neutropenia and infection.

items.label: Addresses TLS risk with allopurinol/rasburicase, hydration and lab monitoring
items.why: 12 cm mass, LDH about 3.6x ULN and rising uric acid put him at risk of tumor lysis.

items.label: Notes 96-hour infusion needs central access; uses existing port
items.why: Continuous infusion of vesicant drugs needs a central line; the port placed 9/18 can be used.

items.label: Offers sperm banking before chemotherapy
items.why: Intensive alkylator and anthracycline chemotherapy can impair fertility in a 54-year-old man.

items.label: Monitors for SVC syndrome or airway compromise; educates patient
items.why: The mediastinal mass narrows the SVC by about 50% and he already has morning facial fullness.

items.label: Confirms HBsAg and anti-HBc nonreactive before rituximab
items.why: Rituximab can reactivate hepatitis B; negative serology means no antiviral is needed.

items.label: Notes baseline LVEF 60% permits anthracycline
items.why: Doxorubicin in the regimen is cardiotoxic; a normal ejection fraction confirms it is safe to give.

items.label: Judges him fit for intensive curative therapy, matching his goal
items.why: Age 54, ECOG 1, normal heart and organ function, and he wants the best chance of cure.
